products.quality: Roster-leading breadth: 10 documented modes (Threshold, Ordered, Atkinson, Dither, Stucki, Jarvis, Newsprint, Halftone with cell size/angle, Grayscale, Sketch); community treats LightBurn as the photo-engraving reference and its dither set as the superset.
CNC-only (no laser): product page lists only CNC control/CAM targets; Phase-0 coverage note confirms no laser functionality, so no laser raster/dither pipeline.

Official docs document a generic '1bit BW dithering' tool without enumerating algorithms; community/third-party writeups list Floyd-Steinberg (default), Jarvis, Stucki, Atkinson, Sierra variants, Burkes, Random. Community: genuinely good for free, trails LightBurn on complex photos.

xTool Studio bitmap modes: Grayscale (default), Bayer, Floyd, Stucki, Atkinson, Jarvis, Sierra, with per-mode guidance (Jarvis recommended for infrared, Grayscale for blue diode). No halftone/newsprint family. Quality beyond docs not established.

Not a laser raster product: Easel Pro's 'Raster Toolpaths' is a CNC pocket-clearing fill strategy (bit moves in parallel lines, X/Y direction only), not image dithering; community confirms Easel is not meant for laser work.

Grayscale mode 'varies power output as a percentage between Min and Max Power' per layer. Community consensus: excellent for depth/3D effects; on diode lasers users often prefer dithering for tonal photos — a material limit, not a software one.
CNC-only; no laser power-modulated engraving (product page lists only CNC targets).

Line To Line tool engraves 'realistic shades of grey' via PWM (laser must support power modulation); S-MIN maps white pixels, S-MAX black; M3/M4 choice documented. Community: close to LightBurn for basic photos; gap widens where fine-tuning matters.

Grayscale is the default xTool Studio bitmap mode ('the darker the pixel, the deeper the carving' — per-pixel power modulation). No documented user control of the power mapping curve or S-min/max equivalent; quality signal beyond docs not established.
No laser pipeline; CNC depth comes from Z, not power modulation. Community: Easel is not meant to drive laser heads.

Adjust Image tool (contrast, brightness, gamma with live preview) plus vector-shape image masking/cropping (Apply Mask to Image; masks stay editable with node/boolean tools, removable non-destructively).
CNC-only; no laser image pipeline to adjust.

Import dialog documents brightness/contrast, B&W threshold, three grayscale conversion formulas (SimpleAverage/WeightAverage/OpticalCorrect) plus custom RGB weights, bicubic/nearest resize, and rotate/crop/flip tools. Color invert was a requested gap (GitHub #130); current status unverified.

xTool Studio documents brightness, contrast, saturation, sharpness, and temperature sliders, bitmap color invert (incl. grayscale/color handling), and stylistic bitmap filters. No gamma control documented.
Raster images are only consumed via Image Trace to vectors; no raster-engrave image-adjustment pipeline exists.

Per-layer Line Interval with linked DPI display controls 'spacing between scanned rows'; separate Cells-per-Inch density for Halftone. Docs and vendor/community guides give material-specific interval guidance.
CNC-only; stepover for milling is a different concept (S7), no laser line-interval control.

Row density set via 'Quality' in lines/mm; official dithering page advises 'use a high quality resolution' for best results. Third-party guides document lines-per-mm behavior; no DPI-unit display documented.

xTool Studio 'Lines per cm' documented with visual 10–300 lines/cm examples; applies to Bitmap and Vector Engrave on all models except F1/F1 Ultra bitmap engrave (fixed resolution there). Metric-only unit; no DPI display documented.
No laser raster pipeline; the analogous CNC control is bit stepover, out of this sector.

Images are first-class canvas objects: documented editable vector masking/crop; scan angle is layer-controlled independent of object orientation. Arbitrary rotate/scale/flip of image objects is inferred from the documented object model, not a fetched doc page — flagged INF.

evidence.cite: https://docs.lightburnsoftware.com/latest/Reference/CutSettingsEditor/ImageMode/ (scan angle documented as a layer setting, implying object transforms are free; free rotation itself not fetch-verified)

products.quality: CNC-only; no raster engrave operation to transform.

Rotate/crop/flip tools documented in the import dialog plus numeric size/offset — but transforms are fixed at G-code conversion; no on-canvas object model afterwards. Arbitrary-angle rotation not documented; users resort to editing images externally.
xTool Studio has full canvas object editing (move/rotate/scale/flip) that applies to bitmap objects per the Object Editing doc; skew/warp not documented.
No raster engrave operation; imported rasters exist only as trace sources.

Deepest documented set: Scan Angle (any angle, 0/90/180 semantics), per-pass Angle Increment, bidirectional toggle, Overscanning, Dot Width Correction, Fill Grouping. Community caveat: non-90-degree angles are emulated with cut moves (style option); DSP advised to 90-degree multiples.
CNC-only; no laser scan-line options.

Conversion direction selectable horizontal/vertical/diagonal (diagonal halves effective axis speed) per community guides; a uni-directional option was a user request (#97). Overscan control not documented anywhere found — treat overscan/bi-di toggle as unknown.

xTool Studio documents uni/bi-directional 'Engraving Mode' (bi-di faster, edges less clean). Engraving angle + cross-hatch documented but gated: XCS V2.3+, currently F1 Ultra vector engraving only. Overscan is machine-managed, not user-exposed.
Raster X/Y direction choice exists only for CNC pocket clearing, not laser scanning.
Both special modes documented per layer: Pass-Through for images 'pre-processed for laser engraving' (skips resampling/dither) and Negative Image inversion for dark materials.
CNC-only; no laser image modes.

No documented pass-through or negative mode on lasergrbl.com; color-invert at import was an open user request (GitHub #130) and Facebook posts discuss unwanted inversion, not a feature. Whether later builds added either is unverified.

Negative covered: bitmap color invert documented for dark/transparent materials (B&W, grayscale, color handling specified). No documented pre-dithered pass-through mode — inferred absent from the bitmap-mode doc set.

evidence.cite: https://support.xtool.com/article/2432 (bitmap mode list contains no pass-through option)

products.quality: No raster engrave pipeline at all, so no special modes.
